messages:
Priya C: Quick heads-up — we need a short, targeted customer comms sequence for this morning's batch-embedding throttle incident. Impacted groups: onboarding batches (low env), scheduled ingest jobs (mid-size), and a handful of high-SLA production tenants. Draft proposal below; please chime with edits.

Alex M: Thanks. Can we 1) segment by impact level, 2) offer a 1-time credit, and 3) schedule live help windows? Prefer short, plain-language first message.

Priya C: Agreed. Proposed segmentation: 
- Level A: production (50 tenants) — priority email + dedicated office hour slot + 10% credit on last invoice
- Level B: scheduled ingest/onboarding (200 tenants) — email + group office hours + 5% credit
- Level C: short retries/unaffected but saw errors (ALL others) — brief status note, no credit but link to FAQ

Jordan K: For renewal-risk accounts we should loop in AMs before sending. Suggest a 1:1 flag to Sales Ops for any tenant with outstanding renewal in 90 days.

Priya C: Good call. Jordan, can Sales Ops produce a list of renewal-window tenants by 11:30?

Sales Ops: Yep, will drop the CSV into #cs-shared by 11:15.

Mateo R: Quick note on tone: avoid deep engineering detail in initial message. Keep a short summary + ETA for RCA. We can attach a technical appendix for customers who ask.

Priya C: Draft email (short):
"Hi <Org> — we experienced a transient throttling issue this morning that impacted batch embedding jobs. We’ve mitigated the root cause and restarted queued jobs; most jobs succeeded by 09:40 PT. We’re offering a one-time credit for affected jobs (details below) and running dedicated office hours to help catch up. Full technical summary and next steps will be posted in a follow-up within 48 hours. Reply to this thread if you need priority help. —Priya, CS"

Alex M: Love it. For Level A mention dedicated queue bumping and optional expedited rerun (ops-assisted).

Priya C: Updated Level A blurb in email: "If you’re Level A, reply and we’ll schedule an expedited rerun with an ops engineer."

Sam L: Legal Bot — should we include any SLA credit language or stick with a goodwill credit?

Legal Bot: Recommend goodwill credit language only: avoid implying SLA breach until the RCA confirms root cause and duration. Phrase: "one-time credit as a gesture of goodwill".

Priya C: Noted. Also planning live help rotations: 
- 10:00–11:00 PT: ops + eng on call (limited 1:1 slots)
- 14:00–15:00 PT: group office hours (walkthrough replay + troubleshooting)
We’ll publish links in the email.

Jordan K: Can we add a short feedback ask and a tiny survey link? We should capture whether they lost revenue or missed SLAs. Keep it 3 questions max.

Priya C: Yes — quick survey: 1) Were you materially impacted? (Y/N) 2) Would you like ops assist? (Y/N) 3) Any immediate blockers? (text)

Mateo R: Final step: engineering to prepare the technical appendix + timeline and draft RCA stub. ETA from eng for appendix?

Alex M: I’ll have a timeline + initial investigation notes by 15:00 PT; full RCA in 48h.

Priya C: Next actions: 
- Sales Ops: list of renewal-window tenants (by 11:15) — @Sales Ops
- Alex: tech appendix + timeline (by 15:00) — @Alex M
- Legal Bot: approve credit wording (ASAP) — @Legal Bot
- Mateo/Jordan: review customer email tone and survey (by 11:45) — @Mateo Ruiz @Jordan K
- CS: send segmented emails after approvals (target 12:30) — @Priya C / @Sam L

Alex M: thumbs up. I’ll post the appendix in this thread when ready.

Priya C: Thanks everyone. If no objections by 11:30 I’ll start sending Level A messages manually (to ensure AMs are looped). :thumbsup:

Sam L: :raised_hands:

Jordan K: Will monitor renewals list when Sales Ops posts it.

Priya C: Posting final draft in #cs-drafts once Legal confirms wording.
